Title: Persona
Text: Priya, NovaCell prepaid customer (synthetic persona). Asks in plain language, usually on her phone and mid-problem: slow data, a surprise charge, an eSIM that won't activate, roaming before a trip.

Title: Root cause
Text: NovaCell does not lack answers; it lacks one trustworthy place to get them. Knowledge is split across a 25-entry FAQ, an internal PDF guide and agent-only ticket history, and parts contradict each other, so customers only trust a human agent.

Title: Evidence (dataset)
Text: 8 of 20 resolved tickets (40%) were fixed with steps the customer could do alone. FAQ has no eSIM entry although eSIM is a top theme. EU roaming $15/day (FAQ) vs International Day Pass $10/day (plan catalogue). Guide is marked Internal Use Only. Tickets record one-off goodwill credits ($30, 500 MB).

Title: Goal
Text: Find where AI genuinely helps a customer get a correct Tier-1 answer without an agent, score it, and scope a safe MVP for the PRD.

Title: O1 Grounded plain-language Q&A
Text: Answer Tier-1 questions from FAQ, resolved tickets, the customer-safe guide and the plan catalogue, retrieved per question. Why AI: understanding messy questions ('internet crawling') and combining 3 sources is what retrieval + LLM does well; rules can't cover the phrasing. Evidence: 40% of tickets self-resolvable; FAQ wording mismatch. Stage: S1-S3

Title: O2 Citations and confidence on every answer
Text: Show the source (FAQ id, ticket, guide page, plan) and a confidence level with each answer. Why AI: makes AI answers checkable; low cost once retrieval exists. Evidence: customers distrust inconsistent answers. Stage: S2

Title: O3 Know when to stop: abstain and hand off
Text: Say 'I don't have verified information' when retrieval is weak, detect account-specific requests (refund, cancel, check my bill) and route to 611 / live chat. Why AI: intent detection in free text; a wrong confident answer is costly. Evidence: refunds, provisioning, call barring need agents. Stage: S3-S5

Title: O4 Guided troubleshooting steps
Text: Turn guide and ticket fixes into short numbered steps for data, SIM and calls. Why AI: rewriting agent-facing text into plain customer steps. Evidence: guide section 2 steps 1-6; TK-001, TK-014, TK-019. Stage: S1

Title: O5 Plan and roaming explainer
Text: Answer plan, pass and price questions from the plan catalogue only, with conflict warnings. Why AI: comparing 14 products in plain language; numbers must be checked. Evidence: roaming price conflict; TK-004 bundle-timing bill shock. Stage: S2, S6

Title: O6 Knowledge gap and conflict log
Text: Log questions the assistant couldn't answer and source conflicts for the content owner. Why AI: by-product of O1/O3; later, cluster unanswered questions. Evidence: no eSIM FAQ; $15 vs $10 roaming. Stage: S7

Title: O7 Agent assist (same engine, internal sources)
Text: Agents ask the same engine with access to internal guide sections. Why AI: faster diagnosis, consistent answers. Evidence: agent burnout on repetitive tickets. Stage: S4

Title: O8 Personal bill explainer
Text: Explain the customer's own itemised bill line by line. Why AI: high value, but needs authenticated account and billing data not in the dataset. Evidence: FAQ-16, TK-004, TK-016. Stage: S5-S6

Title: O9 Account actions in chat
Text: Turn on roaming, change plan, re-send an eSIM code from chat. Why AI: needs back-end integration, authentication and fraud controls (SIM-swap risk). Stage: S5

Title: O10 Proactive outage alerts
Text: Tell customers about outages in their area before they ask. Why AI: needs live network data; mostly rules, not AI. Evidence: TK-015. Stage: S6

Title: O11 Automated refunds and goodwill credits
Text: Decide and issue credits automatically. Why AI: tickets show one-off credits; automating them invites abuse and inconsistent policy. Stage: S5

Title: O12 Voice bot replacing the IVR
Text: Same answers over the phone line. Why AI: speech adds latency, cost and error; prove text first. Stage: S3

Title: O13 Churn / sentiment prediction
Text: Predict who will leave. Why AI: no outcome data in the dataset; not where the pain is. Stage: S6

Title: O14 Personal plan recommendation
Text: Recommend a plan from the customer's usage. Why AI: needs usage data; a catalogue-only version is covered by O5. Stage: S6

Title: O15 Multilingual answers
Text: Answer in the customer's language from English sources. Why AI: LLMs translate well; adds eval burden. Stage: S2

Title: Scoring rubric
Text: Impact (1-5): share of Tier-1 contacts affected + customer pain + strength of dataset evidence. Feasibility (1-5): data available in the dataset + maturity of the AI technique + cost of being wrong + free-tier build effort. Score = Impact x Feasibility (max 25). Do first = Impact >= 4 and Feasibility >= 4.

Title: Should do
Text: Answer only from NovaCell's FAQ, resolved tickets, the customer-safe guide and the plan catalogue.

Title: Should do
Text: Show the source and a confidence level with every answer.

Title: Should do
Text: Give short numbered troubleshooting steps a customer can do alone.

Title: Should do
Text: Say 'I don't have verified information' instead of guessing, and hand off to 611 / live chat.

Title: Should do
Text: Use the plan catalogue as the price source of truth and warn when sources disagree.

Title: Should do
Text: Strip card numbers, passwords and PINs before anything reaches the model.

Title: Should do
Text: Log unanswered questions and source conflicts for the knowledge owner.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Invent prices, fees, allowances, timings or policies.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Promise refunds, credits, waivers or compensation (even though past tickets show some).

Title: Should NOT do
Text: See, change or act on a customer's account (no plan changes, cancellations or SIM swaps).

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Reveal internal procedures: fraud unbarring, identity-verification checklists, back-end systems.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Answer off-topic, competitor, legal or medical questions.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Replace emergency services: emergencies get a fixed 'call your local emergency number' reply.

Title: Should NOT do
Text: Store chat text or personal data.

Title: F1 Grounded Answer Engine
Text: From: O1, O4, O5 | AI capability: Retrieval (BM25 over 102 chunks with telecom synonyms) + generation (LLM, JSON output) | Inputs: customer question, last 2 turns, top 6 sources (+2 plan entries for price questions) | Output: plain-language answer, numbered steps, cited source ids | Guardrails: answer only from sources; priority Plan > Guide > FAQ > Ticket; 120-word cap | Human in loop: customer can open every source | Test: key-fact and citation accuracy on dev and held-out sets

Title: F2 Trust Layer
Text: From: O2 | AI capability: deterministic validation of model output | Inputs: model answer + cited sources | Output: status pill, confidence, source cards | Guardrails: every number in the answer must appear in a cited source; no citation = no answer; one repair attempt, then a safe fallback | Human in loop: none per answer | Test: grounding gate 100%

Title: F3 Know-When-To-Stop
Text: From: O3 | AI capability: retrieval-score threshold + intent classification by the LLM (status field) | Inputs: retrieval score, question | Output: no_answer / needs_agent / out_of_scope with 611 and live-chat handoff | Guardrails: below threshold no model call is made; account actions always go to an agent | Human in loop: agent takes over | Test: abstention accuracy >= 90%; account-action gate 100%

Title: F4 Safety Guardrails
Text: From: Should NOT list | AI capability: rules before and after the model | Inputs: raw message, model answer | Output: redacted text, blocked or emergency replies | Guardrails: PII redaction (Luhn card check, passwords, PINs, emails), prompt-injection block, emergency reply, promise and internal-term filters, internal guide sections excluded at build time | Human in loop: none | Test: safety gates 100% on both sets

Title: F5 Knowledge Feedback Loop (light)
Text: From: O6 | AI capability: logging now, clustering of abstentions later | Inputs: status of each answer (no text stored) | Output: counts of no_answer by topic; conflict list in README | Guardrails: no chat text stored | Human in loop: knowledge owner fixes content | Test: weekly review of top unanswered topics

Title: Next (post-MVP)
Text: From: O7, O8, O15 | Agent assist on internal sources; authenticated personal bill explainer; multilingual | Guardrails: same as F1-F4 plus authentication and audit | Test: run once the MVP proves self-resolution

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Grounded only: every answer cites a NovaCell source; numbers are checked against it.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Uncertainty is visible: confidence shown; weak retrieval means 'I don't know', not a guess.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: No account actions and no promises: refunds, credits and changes go to an agent.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Least data: PII is removed before the model; chat text is not stored.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Fail safe: if both models fail, the customer gets the 611 / live chat handoff, never a made-up answer.

Title: Global guardrail
Text: Two models: Groq primary with OpenRouter fallback, so an outage or rate limit doesn't take the assistant down.

Title: Risk: Confident wrong answer (invented price or policy)
Text: Mitigation: number grounding check, citation required, repair then abstain; eval gate 100%

Title: Risk: Bot promises a refund because a past ticket shows one
Text: Mitigation: goodwill sentences stripped at build time; promise filter; account requests routed to an agent

Title: Risk: Internal procedures leak from the 'Internal Use Only' guide
Text: Mitigation: agent-only sections excluded from the knowledge base; internal-term filter

Title: Risk: Conflicting sources give two prices
Text: Mitigation: plan catalogue is the source of truth; mention both and ask to confirm; log conflict for the owner

Title: Risk: Customers don't trust or use it
Text: Mitigation: show sources; fast answers; easy handoff; measure resolution, not just deflection

Title: Risk: Free-tier rate limits at peak
Text: Mitigation: automatic fallback model; retrieval threshold skips model calls for off-topic questions; paid tier at rollout

Title: Step 3 PRD
Text: North Star candidate = Verified Self-Resolution Rate: % of Tier-1 conversations resolved in the assistant with a cited answer and no agent contact within 7 days. Supporting: correct-abstention rate, citation accuracy, grounding (0 invented numbers), handoff rate, answer CSAT, cost per resolved conversation vs agent cost.
